messages:
maria (support): Heads-up — ACME reported a steady stream of 5xxs against hosted inference since ~2026-03-10 11:22 UTC. They're seeing generation requests fail mid-stream (customers get 503). I filed INC-2026-042 and started a call with them.

ajay (sre): I'm seeing a spike in 503 responses at the gateway around 11:20-11:40 UTC, correlated with a dependent service (cache-service) rolling update. Upstream shows a mix of 502 and 504 from the cache cluster.

lucy (backend): We deployed a small kvcache change at 11:18 that updated eviction TTL handling. Rolling update succeeded, but there were short windows of elevated latency on the cache pods. Possible hot-path regression.

maria (support): Customer says SDK retried aggressively and they reported duplicate billing tokens. They want immediate mitigation + status for comms.

tom (infra): I'm going to pause the rolling update and roll back cache-service to previous revision. Starting rollback now. Will also adjust LB drain/connection settings.\
deploy-bot: rollback cache-service v2.7.1 -> v2.7.0 initiated by tom at 11:33 UTC :arrow_backward:

ajay (sre): Repro snippet from our curl test against tenant-specific route:

```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```

When it fails, response looks like:

```
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2026 11:24:21 GMT
Content-Type: application/json

{"error":{"message":"upstream unavailable","code":503}}
```

SDK log (node) from customer: `redwood-js@1.8.0` shows: `RequestError: 503 Service Unavailable` then 5 retries with exponential backoff. They had maxRetries=5 configured.

customer_ops: Customer says they were billed for two full responses because the SDK retried and the gateway accepted the subsequent request once the upstream recovered. They want a credit if costs > X.

lucy (backend): Temporary mitigation suggestions:
- Enable per-tenant routing fallback to a lighter model (redwood-small) for ACME so we avoid cache pressure.
- Limit SDK retries server-side for this tenant (circuit breaker) to avoid duplicate forwardings.
- Backpressure: reduce ingress concurrency for that tenant.

ajay (sre): Implemented two mitigations at 11:40 UTC: added tenant routing override -> redwood-small and set a tenant-level circuit-breaker (max_inflight=4, max_retries=2). Also set HTTP connection timeout shorter for streaming window.

incidents-bot: INC-2026-042 updated: mitigations applied at 11:40 UTC. Priority: high.

maria (support): I sent ACME this note: "We observed a dependency regression during a cache-service rollout that caused transient 5xxs. We've applied a tenant-specific fallback to a smaller model and reduced retry amplification while we roll back the cache change. We'll follow up with a remediation timeline and investigate billing impact." They acknowledged and asked for ETA.

tom (infra): Rollback completed at 11:45 UTC. Metrics post-rollback: gateway 5xx rate dropped from ~12% to ~0.9% in 5m window. Returning to normal p95.

ryan (eng): Can someone attach the request traces and kvcache logs for the impacted window (11:15-11:50)? Need to see whether eviction logic caused hot-cache misses and cascading timeouts. Also want the exact SDK request IDs to correlate billing.

ajay (sre): Pushed a Grafana snapshot and trace links to the incident (https://grafana.internal/shot/INC-2026-042). Key observations: small spike in kvcache 99th latency from 180ms -> 1.8s during the pod restart flurry. A subset of requests timed out and caused gateway fallback loop.

lucy (backend): Repro steps for qa (local emulation):
1) Start kvcache with TTL change: `CACHE_TTL=30s`
2) Seed cache with heavy keys (use load script)
3) Trigger rolling restart of cache pods with `kubectl rollout restart deploy/kvcache`
4) Run concurrent generate requests (concurrency 50) to the tenant route for 2 minutes.
Expected: a portion of requests will hit cold cache, spike backend latency, and show 5xx at gateway.

maria (support): For customer comms: we'll offer a billing credit for duplicate tokens due to our retry/acceptance window and provide a follow-up in 2 hours with root-cause and remediation. I'll draft the billing note after we get exact token counts.

customer_ops: Please include a short how-to for the customer to temporarily set client-side `maxRetries` to 1 while we finish rollback — they can also pin to a model alias that we set (redwood-small).

ajay (sre): Post-rollback status check at 11:52 UTC: failure rate stable <1%, streaming success ratio back to baseline, circuit-breaker not tripped. Leaving tenant routing override active for 2h as safety.

maria (support): Thanks team — I'll keep ACME updated. Next steps: postmortem with timeline + code/infra fix (ensure rolling update safety for kvcache and add tenancy throttles), and a billing reconciliation for duplicates.

ryan (eng): I'll own the postmortem. Assigning action items:
- lucy: root-cause patch for TTL behavior and improved telemetry on eviction (ETA 2 days)
- ajay: add automatic tenant circuit-breaker config rollout (ETA 3 days)
- tom: review deployment strategy for cache-service (graceful-drain improvement) (ETA 4 days)

maria (support): ACME replied :thumbsup: and said they appreciate the quick rollback & fallback. Closing temporary communications loop; will follow with billing note once numbers available.

ajay (sre): Minor note — we should add a sentinel that detects kvcache latency > 500ms during rollouts and auto-hold further rolling updates. Adding to backlog.

lucy (backend): Will include specific log markers (tenant_id + req_id) in next kvcache release to speed tracing.

maria (support): Closing thread for now — status: mitigated, rollback done, tenant fallback active until 13:40 UTC, postmortem assigned.

(incidents-bot): INC-2026-042 status -> mitigated; follow-up in 2h for billing update.
